other.label: CBO cost estimate: H.R. 5366, Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act

summary: The Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act amends the Internal Revenue Code to codify and extend tax relief rules for individuals affected by major disasters and certain wildfires. It allows individuals to deduct qualified personal casualty losses arising from major disasters with incident periods beginning before January 1, 2027, and excludes qualified wildfire relief payments from gross income for forest or range fires declared as federal disasters after 2014 and before 2027.

affected_groups.effect: May deduct unreimbursed personal casualty losses exceeding $500 per casualty, including those who do not itemize deductions.
Exclude compensation for losses, expenses, or damages from certain forest or range fires from their gross income regardless of when received, provided the disaster was declared between 2014 and 2027.
affected_groups.group: Recipients of qualified wildfire relief payments

key_provisions: Extends the federal tax deduction for qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses by defining a qualified disaster area as an area where a major disaster was declared with an incident period beginning on or after December 28, 2019, and before January 1, 2027.
Sets the dollar limitation for qualified disaster-related personal casualty losses at $500.
Allows the personal casualty loss deduction for individuals who do not elect to itemize deductions.
Excludes qualified wildfire relief payments from gross income when received for forest or range fires declared as federal disasters after 2014 and before 2027.
Prevents double benefits by denying deductions, credits, or basis increases for expenditures covered by excluded wildfire relief payments.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act amends the Internal Revenue Code to codify and extend tax relief rules for individuals affected by major disasters and certain wildfires. It allows individuals to deduct qualified personal casualty losses arising from major disasters with incident periods beginning before January 1, 2027, and excludes qualified wildfire relief payments from gross income for forest or range fires declared as federal disasters after 2014 and before 2027.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation establishes permanent statutory authority and extends timelines for specific tax relief provisions benefiting individuals impacted by major disasters and wildfires.
